answer: Edge-Density Quota. Each identity is assigned a cipher-derived routing neighborhood; agents must maintain a minimum count of distinct, reciprocally-verified neighbors at distance two before their actions carry weight. An attacker spinning up identities must fund real relay traffic and latency through each one to build that sparse opal of edges, and isolated clusters get flagged by their ridge-like degree profile and down-weighted. Cost: sustained bandwidth and compute per fake identity, growing with every added node.
